subject.title: Install ClawHub packages for new Claw agents

question: Should experimental `claws add` be permitted to install or reuse process-wide plugins under the displayed per-Claw plan consent, or must that action require a separate host-level grant or be deferred?
rationale: Code can preserve integrity and provenance, but it cannot determine whether a single Claw creation flow should be authorized to alter the shared plugin runtime for sibling agents.

options.title: Require a host-level grant
options.body: Keep plugin support, but require an explicit host-scoped acknowledgement in addition to the exact Claw plan before process-wide plugin mutation.

options.title: Defer shared plugins
options.body: Land the workspace-scoped skill path only and leave plugin package actions blocked until a separate shared-host lifecycle contract is accepted.

options.title: Accept current experimental consent
options.body: Treat the displayed exact plan as sufficient authority for shared plugin installation while retaining the experimental gate and warnings.

recommendation.title: Require a host-level grant
recommendation.body: Keep plugin support, but require an explicit host-scoped acknowledgement in addition to the exact Claw plan before process-wide plugin mutation.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review identifies the unresolved shared-runtime authority boundary and the relevant consumer impact.
